If sentiment is negative or neutral in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending upward, cap mid-horizon (8–15 days) at 1.5% above recent peak to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, apply 0.5% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect diminishing momentum.  
When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% across all horizons to reflect bearish drift.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00+ and forecast is rising, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in early horizon to capture bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is volatile, apply 0.5% smoothing filter across all horizons to dampen noise.
